label: database-row-insert-attributed
notes: Same scenario and same iteration count as the baseline it supersedes, so
the totals are directly comparable. What is new is per-endpoint
attribution of the slope.
`a51f31b2` made the v2 owner projection ~9x cheaper per row (246us -> 27us,
measured directly against the index). It moved this scenario's growth
ratio not at all: 1.58-1.67 here against 1.48-1.84 before. That is not a
failed change, it is a mis-aimed one — the projection was ~0.22ms of a
~1.3ms/row end-to-end slope, so removing 9/10 of it is inside the noise.
The attribution metrics exist so the next attempt is aimed at something
measured. Averaged over the three runs, of the +51.7ms a write picks up
between the first and last quarter of the table: mutate +35.3ms (68%),
the client gap between responses +12.0ms (23%), describe +2.7ms (5%),
query +1.7ms (3%).
So the write endpoint holds the slope, and it is remarkably stable about
it — mutate grows 1.89x/2.01x/2.03x across the three runs. The index
refresh is no longer a meaningful part of that; the remaining ~0.88ms/row
is the rest of the write path (owner reserialization, the shadow-repo
commit, the durable journal entry), none of which has been measured yet.
rowInsertMedianMs is submit -> the first read-back that started after the
write landed. Runs are only comparable at the same iteration count.
Captured with OK_PERF_ROW_ITERATIONS=40 against a restarted dev server, so
the API process is running the code under test rather than whatever was
loaded when the server started.
